events.title: Prophet Muhammad dies in Medina
events.description: Muhammad died in Medina, by most traditions on this day. Within a generation his successors, the caliphs, had carried Islam from Arabia to Persia and North Africa.
events.html: Muhammad died in Medina, by most traditions on this day. Within a generation his successors, the caliphs, had carried Islam from Arabia to Persia and North Africa.

events.title: Vikings raid the monastery of Lindisfarne
events.description: Norse raiders attacked the island monastery off Northumbria, killing monks and seizing treasure. The shock across Christian Europe has made the raid a symbolic start of the Viking Age.
events.html: Norse raiders attacked the island monastery off Northumbria, killing monks and seizing treasure. The shock across Christian Europe has made the raid a symbolic start of the Viking Age.

events.title: Richard the Lionheart arrives at the siege of Acre
events.description: Richard I joined the crusaders besieging Acre, which surrendered five weeks later. He went on to win at Arsuf but never retook Jerusalem.
events.html: Richard I joined the crusaders besieging Acre, which surrendered five weeks later. He went on to win at Arsuf but never retook Jerusalem.

events.title: Andrew Jackson dies at the Hermitage
events.description: The seventh US president died at his Tennessee plantation aged 78. Victor at New Orleans and champion of the 'common man', he also drove the forced removal of Native Americans.
events.html: The seventh US president died at his Tennessee plantation aged 78. Victor at New Orleans and champion of the 'common man', he also drove the forced removal of Native Americans.

events.title: Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four is published
events.description: Secker and Warburg published George Orwell's novel of a totalitarian surveillance state. Terms such as 'Big Brother' and 'doublethink' passed into everyday language.
events.html: Secker and Warburg published George Orwell's novel of a totalitarian surveillance state. Terms such as 'Big Brother' and 'doublethink' passed into everyday language.

events.title: James Earl Ray is arrested at Heathrow
events.description: Martin Luther King's killer was caught at London Heathrow travelling on a false Canadian passport. He pleaded guilty in 1969 and was sentenced to 99 years.

intl.name: World Oceans Day
intl.description: Officially recognised by the United Nations in 2008, World Oceans Day highlights the ocean's critical role in sustaining life on Earth and promotes global action to protect marine ecosystems from pollution and overexploitation.
